(CONFIDENTIAL) LICENSE AGREEMENT Date: i dj , 2011 The following provisions are an integral part of this License Agreement, and may be hereinafter supplemented.
1. LICENSOR: 100 OAKS PLAZA LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ADDRESS: 12770 Coit Road, Suite 810 Dallas, Texas 75251 CONTACT: - Laura Steeger TELEPHONE NUMBER: 214-273-3600 Laura@atrdallas.com All correspondence sent to LICENSOR shall be sent with copy to: [Insert name, title and address here, if applicable]
2. LICENSEE: Nashville Farmers Market ADDRESS: 900 Rosa L. Parks Blvd. Nashville, Tennessee 37208 Jeff.themm@nashville.gov ATTENTION: Jeff Themm TELEPHONE: 615-880-2001, Ext 26 FACSIMILE: 615-880-2000
3. LICENSE AREA (“PREMISES”): Farmers' Market will be located in the common area of 100 Oaks Shopping Center (the "Shopping Center"); specifically, in the parking lot on the south side of the ROSS store, close to the MTA bus stop.
4. TERM AND TERMINATION: The term shall commence on or about June 2, 2011 and end on or about October 27, 2011. LICENSOR may revoke this License at any time by giving written notice to LICENSEE. This License Agreement shall automatically terminate in the event of: the revocation, suspension, non-renewal, termination or other restriction of any necessary State of Tennessee permit and/or license for LICENSEE to operate its Farmers’ Market. LICENSEE’S TRADE NAME: Nashville Farmers' Market . USE: LICENSEE shall use the PREMISES solely for the operation of a Farmers’ Market, subject to terms and conditions as set forth herein (“Farmers’ Market”). ARCHIVE
(CONFIDENTIAL)
7. COSTS: This License Agreement is created in the interest of providing a benefit to the community, and no monetary fee is owed to LICENSOR by LICENSEE for use of the Premises to operate the Farmers’ Market described herein.
8. HOURS OF OPERATION: During the term of this Agreement, the Premises shall be operated as a Farmers’ Market on specific days and during the hours of operation specified to that market and location. The parties shall schedule in advance specific days for the Farmers’ Market that are mutually agreeable to both parties, and shall confirm all such scheduled days in writing. LICENSEE shall notify LICENSOR at least five (5) days in advance, unless for severe inclement weather, if LICENSEE will not be operating the Farmers’ Market on a date already scheduled with LICENSOR.
9. SELECTION AND PRICING: LICENSEE shall be responsible for the selection of vendors and rental rates for the Farmers’ Market. LICENSEE shall deliver a list of potential vendors and LICENSOR shall approve the list within 30 days of receiving said list. Ifthe list is not approved within the 30 days, it will be deemed automatically approved. However, LICENSEE agrees to terminate the license agreement with any vendor, if any merchandise item is identified by LICENSOR to be inappropriate for sale on the Premises. LICENSEE agrees that LICENSOR has no responsibility, liability, or obligation associated with any monetary transactions that occur between LICENSEE and any vendors or customers.
10. RULES AND REGULATIONS: LICENSEE shall manage and operate the Farmers’ Market in compliance with applicable policies of LICENSOR as may be in effect from time to time; observe and conform to all laws, rules and regulations, customs and ethics relating to LICENSEE 's business operation; and comply with all state and federal statutes, rules, regulations and policies. LICENSOR will deliver a copy of LICENSOR'S policies to LICENSEE.
11. GOVERNMENTAL APPROVALS / FEES: LICENSEE agrees it will not use or suffer or permit any person or persons to use the Premises or any part thereof for any purpose other than for a Market or for any purpose in violation of the laws, ordinances, regulations and requirements of the City and County in which the Premises is situated or other lawful authorities. LICENSEE shall, at its sole cost and expense, procure all permits, licenses and approvals necessary from governmental authorities or others to permit the Premises to be used for the purposes intended herein and shall provide copies of such documents to LICENSOR prior to execution of this Agreement. Should any governmental taxing authority acting under any present or future law, ordinance, or regulation, levy, assess, or impose a tax, excise and/or assessment (other than new income or franchise tax) upon or against this License, the execution hereof and/or the rentals payable by LICENSEE to LICENSOR, either by way of substitution for or in addition to any existing tax on land and buildings or otherwise, and whether or not evidenced by documentary stamps or the like, LICENSEE agrees to be responsible for and to pay such tax, excise and/or assessment, or to reimburse LICENSOR for the amount thereof, as the case may ARCHIVE
(CONFIDENTIAL)
12. MAINTENANCE OF PREMISES: a. During the term hereof, LICENSEE shall keep the Premises and common area of the Shopping Center within a 50’ radius of the Premises in a clean and wholesome condition, free of any objectionable noises, odors or nuisances (in the sole judgment of LICENSOR) and LICENSEE shall comply fully with all health, safety and police regulations. If LICENSEE fails to do so, LICENSOR shall have the right to do so and LICENSEE shall reimburse LICENSOR for the cost thereof. In the event LICENSEE fails to remove any merchandise, inventory, furniture, goods, wares or other property located in or on the Premises after the Farmers’ Market hours, LICENSOR may retain all such property at the Premises or dispose of such property at its sole discretion without any liability to LICENSOR. b. LICENSEE shall collect and remove from LICENSOR’s premises any and all trash generated by or related to the Farmers’ Market and shall not dump any said trash into LICENSOR’s dumpster, trashcans, or street gutters. LICENSEE shall ensure that no wastewater or other liquids, trash, etc. from the Farmers’ Market is dumped into the street gutters or storm drains. Wastewater or other liquids include water used to wash produce, water flowers, etc. c. LICENSEE shall ensure that no vehicles and/or activities associated with the Farmers’ Market will block any of the entrances or exits between the Premises and the street, or any of the interior driveways in the Shopping Center.
13. ALTERATIONS: LICENSOR makes no representation to LICENSEE as to the suitability of the Premises for the purposes contained herein and LICENSEE accepts the Premises in “as | is” condition. LICENSOR shall have no obligation at any time during the term of this | Agreement to make any changes or repairs to or improvements of the Licensed Premises. LICENSEE shall not make, or suffer or permit to be made, any alterations to the Premises without the prior written approval of LICENSOR. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, LICENSEE agrees that no nails, screws, bolts, spikes, pins or other objects will be driven into the pavement, sidewalks, buildings, or other improvements in the Shopping Center. .
14. PROMOTION AND ADVERTISING: LICENSOR shall create all advertising related to the Farmers’ Market, and LICENSEE may display or distribute such advertising, as agreed by LICENSOR. LICENSEE shall not dispense handbills or other forms of advertising anywhere on the Shopping Center without the prior written consent of LICENSOR.
15. EMPLOYEES OF LICENSEE: a. LICENSEE may, at its own expense, employ and train employees to operate its Farmers’ Market. LICENSEE shall be solely responsible for and pay all costs and compensation including salaries, withholding taxes, and unemployment insurance associated with the employment of its employees. ARCHIVE
(CONFIDENTIAL) b. LICENSEE shall give prompt and reasonable attention to written notification from LICENSOR that one or more persons employed by LICENSEE is not acceptable to LICENSOR because of such person’s conduct, actions or demeanor while working at the Farmers’ Market and that in the reasonable opinion of LICENSOR, the removal of such person or persons is necessary to avoid damage to the business or reputation of LICENSOR. Grounds for any such notice may include, but not by way of limitation, intoxication or the use of, or appearance of, being under the influence of alcohol or other controlled substances while on duty at the Farmers’ Market site.
16. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR STATUS: a. LICENSEE is an independent contractor that engages in the operation of its own business and nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to establish a relationship of agent, employee, partnership, association or joint venture between the parties. It is expressly understood that LICENSEE shall be fully and solely responsible for paying, reporting and withholding all taxes relating to any compensation received under this Agreement, including any and all payroll related taxes and legally required tax withholding, for itself and any employees or associates. b, The parties further agree that neither LICENSEE nor any of its associates or employees are employees of LICENSOR for any purpose. Accordingly, LICENSEE, its associates or employees shall not be entitled to nor shall receive from LICENSOR vacation pay, holiday pay, sick leave, life and/or disability insurance coverage, or any other benefit normally provided by an employer to an employee. c. LICENSEE warrants that it shall purchase all goods and materials and make all contracts under its own credit and in its own name. LICENSEE further agrees that it will not make any express or implied representation to third persons inconsistent with the foregoing understanding, and agrees not to represent itself as being associated with LICENSOR in any way other than as specified in this Agreement. LICENSEE. shall not use LICENSOR’s name, brand name, trademark or statements made by or attributed to any of LICENSOR’s employees without the written permission of LICENSOR.
17. Intentionally deleted.
18. INSURANCE: The LICENSEE is a self-insured, metropolitan form of government. LICENSEE must provide a self-insured statement in a letter or memorandum acceptable to the LICENSOR. During the term:of this Agreement, subcontractors of LICENSEE shall maintain the following insurance coverage with limits not less than the amount specified and, if subcontracting is permitted, LICENSEE shall require its subcontractor to maintain similar insurance coverage whenever subcontractors’ personnel are present at the Shopping Center: a. The Licensee's sub contractors shall have and maintain Workers Compensation Insurance conforming with the requirements of the laws of Tennessee. ARCHIVE
(CONFIDENTIAL) -b. Commercial General Liability insurance for bodily injury, property damage including products and completed operations, and personal and advertising injury with minimum limits of $1,000,000 each occurrence. c. Automobile liability insurance (including owned, non-owned, and hired vehicles with a combined single limit for bodily injury, death, and property damage of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence. LICENSOR must be included as additional insured on the general liability and auto policies. LICENSEE shall furnish LICENSOR with certificates of insurance, which provide sufficient information to verify that subcontractors of LICENSEE have complied with the insurance requirements of this Section. Such certificates shall indicate that LICENSOR will be given at ~ Teast thirty (30) advance written notice of any material change or cancellation of any policy and that the required waiver of subrogation or additional insured has been endorsed on the applicable policies. LICENSEE shall not commence any operations on the Premises or permit its subcontractors to do so until the required insurance is obtained and acceptable certificates are delivered to LICENSOR.
19. NONDISCRIMINATION AND EMPLOYEE RIGHTS: LICENSEE will provide services to customers and hire employees without discrimination on account of race, sex, sexual orientation, color, religion, national origin, age, physical or mental handicap, or veteran's status. 21, FORCE MAJEURE: Neither party shall be liable for a delay in its performance of its obligations and responsibilities under this Agreement due to extraordinary causes beyond its | control, such as but not limited to war, act of terrorism, embargo, national emergency, | insurrection or riot, acts of the public enemy, fire, flood or other natural disaster provided that said party has taken reasonable measures to notify the other, in writing, of the delay. Failure of subcontractors and inability to obtain materials (unless such subcontractors and/or materials are specified by LICENSOR or a subcontractor or material supplier is unable to perform for the above-specified reasons) shall not be considered as a force majeure delay. Further, in the event either party is unable to meet its obligations hereunder because of such force majeure, and such inability continues for a period of 30 days or more, then either party may terminate this Agreement effective immediately.
22. HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES: LICENSEE shall not cause or allow the release, generation, use, treatment, storage, or disposal of Hazardous Substances on or near the Premises. “Hazardous Substances” shall mean (i) any substance defined as such in the Comprehensive Environment Response, Compensation and Liability Act (“CERCLA”), 42 U.S.C. 9601 et seq., as amended, (ii) any hazardous waste or hazardous substance as those terms are defined in any local, state or federal law, regulation and ordinance applicable to the Premises, or (iii) petroleum, including crude oil or any fraction thereof. ARCHIVE
(CONFIDENTIAL) .
23. APPLICABLE LAW: This Agreement shall be construed and the legal relations between the parties determined in accordance with the laws of the state of Tennessee and the venue for any formal action initiated in connection with this Agreement shall be in Nashville, Davidson County, Tennessee.
24. NON-EXCLUSIVE AGREEMENT: This Agreement is nonexclusive. LICENSOR reserves the right to lease or license space to any other individual or party to install and operate a Farmers’ Market or any other business operation on the Shopping Center, provided such lease or license does not conflict or compete with LICENSEE’s scheduled Farmers’ Market dates.
25. ENTIRE AGREEMENT: This Agreement contains the entire agreement between the parties. All prior understandings and agreements between the parties relating to the subject matter of this Agreement, not expressly set forth herein, are of no force and effect. This Agreement may be changed or modified only by a writing executed by both parties.
26. NOTICES: Unless expressly provided otherwise, all notices herein provided to be given, or which may be given, by any party to the other, will be deemed to have been fully given when written and personally delivered or deposited in the United States mail, certified and postage prepaid or delivered by overnight delivery service with written proof of delivery, and addressed as indicated in Sections 1 and 2 of this Agreement. Any party that changes its address shall notify, promptly in writing, the other party of its new address. [THE REMAINDER OF THIS PAGE IS INTENTIONALLY LEFT BLANK] ARCHIVE
